Intention-to-diagnose (3x2) analysis

Source: R/dx_itd.R
dx_itd.Rd

Summarize a diagnostic test when some predictions are missing, for example because a case failed quality control or a pre-defined rule stopped the model from running. Instead of excluding these cases, a missing prediction is treated as an ungradable result. Results are summarized in a 3x2 table, with positive, negative, and ungradable test results in the rows and the reference standard in the columns (Schuetz et al., 2012).

Usage

dx_itd(
  data,
  pred_varname,
  true_varname,
  setthreshold = 0.5,
  poslabel = 1,
  grouping_variables = NA,
  citype = "exact"
)

Arguments

data

A tbl.

pred_varname

Column name containing the predictions (string). Values should be predicted probabilities that the outcome is 1, between 0 and 1. Missing values (NA) are ungradable results.

true_varname

Column name containing the reference standard (string). Values should be 0 or 1 (numeric, logical, factor, or character), with no missing values, and both classes must be present.

setthreshold

A number between 0 and 1 representing the threshold used to classify the predictions. Predictions at or above the threshold predict outcome 1.

poslabel

The outcome class that is the event: 1 (default) or 0. Predictions are still probabilities that the outcome is 1, so with poslabel = 0 a prediction below the threshold is a positive test.

grouping_variables

Character vector of variable names to be summarized by. Variables are converted to factors if not already one. A column can't be named "Overall", which is used for the results of all cases.

citype

Confidence interval type for proportions: one of the methods of binom::binom.confint(), such as "exact" (default), "wilson", or "ac".

Value

An object of class dx_itd, a list with data, options, measures (a data frame with one row per measure), and cm (the 3x2 cell counts at setthreshold).

Details

With TP, FN, and UP the positive, negative, and ungradable results among cases with the event, and FP, TN, and UN the same among cases without it:

MeasureDefinition
Diagnostic yield (disease positive)(TP + FN) / (TP + FN + UP)
Diagnostic yield (disease negative)(FP + TN) / (FP + TN + UN)
Diagnostic yield (overall)Gradable results / N
Pre-test disease risk(TP + FN + UP) / N
Positive predictive valueTP / (TP + FP)
Negative predictive valueTN / (TN + FN)
Post-test disease risk (positive)TP / (TP + FP)
Post-test disease risk (negative)FN / (TN + FN)
Post-test disease risk (ungradable)UP / (UP + UN)
Likelihood ratio (positive)(TP / (TP + FN + UP)) / (FP / (FP + TN + UN))
Likelihood ratio (negative)(FN / (TP + FN + UP)) / (TN / (FP + TN + UN))
Likelihood ratio (ungradable)(UP / (TP + FN + UP)) / (UN / (FP + TN + UN))
Worst-case sensitivityTP / (TP + FN + UP)
Worst-case specificityTN / (FP + TN + UN)
Worst-case Youden's JWorst-case sensitivity + worst-case specificity - 1

Diagnostic yield is the proportion of cases with a gradable (positive or negative) result. The worst case counts every ungradable result as incorrect: as a negative result for cases with the event, and as a positive result for cases without it. Predictive values only use gradable results.

The likelihood ratios use all cases with and without the event as denominators, including ungradable results, so the positive and negative likelihood ratios differ from dx_lrt_pos() and dx_lrt_neg() on the gradable cases. A likelihood ratio near 1 for ungradable results means they are about as common with and without the event.

Proportions use binomial confidence intervals (citype). Likelihood ratios use a large sample interval on the log scale. If the 2x2 table of one row against the others has a zero cell, 0.5 is added to each of its cells. Youden's J uses a Wald interval that treats the two outcome classes as independent, truncated to -1 to 1. The interval is too narrow when the worst-case sensitivity or specificity is 0% or 100%, and has no width when both are, which is noted in the results. Likelihood ratios are NA for a result no case has, such as ungradable results when no predictions are missing.

At least one prediction is needed, but a subgroup in grouping_variables can have every prediction missing, for example a site where every case failed quality control. It is kept with a warning, with a diagnostic yield of 0%.

References

Schuetz GM, Schlattmann P, Dewey M. Use of 3x2 tables with an intention to diagnose approach to assess clinical performance of diagnostic tests: meta-analytical evaluation of coronary CT angiography studies. BMJ. 2012;345:e6717.

See also

dx_itd_table() for the 3x2 table, dx() when every prediction is available.

Examples

data <- dx_heart_failure
data$predicted[seq(5, 261, by = 20)] <- NA
fit <- dx_itd(data, pred_varname = "predicted", true_varname = "truth")
summary(fit)
#> 
#> 
#> Table: Threshold= 0.5
#> 
#> |variable |label   |measure                             |summary              |
#> |:--------|:-------|:-----------------------------------|:--------------------|
#> |Overall  |Overall |Diagnostic Yield (Disease Positive) |94.9% (88.5%, 98.3%) |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Diagnostic Yield (Disease Negative) |95.1% (90.6%, 97.9%) |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Diagnostic Yield (Overall)          |95.0% (91.6%, 97.3%) |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Pre-Test Disease Risk               |37.5% (31.7%, 43.7%) |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Positive Predictive Value           |84.6% (74.7%, 91.8%) |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Negative Predictive Value           |84.1% (77.7%, 89.3%) |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Post-Test Disease Risk (Positive)   |84.6% (74.7%, 91.8%) |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Post-Test Disease Risk (Negative)   |15.9% (10.7%, 22.3%) |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Post-Test Disease Risk (Ungradable) |38.5% (13.9%, 68.4%) |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Likelihood Ratio (Positive)         |9.15 (5.22, 16.04)   |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Likelihood Ratio (Negative)         |0.31 (0.23, 0.44)    |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Likelihood Ratio (Ungradable)       |1.04 (0.35, 3.09)    |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Worst-Case Sensitivity              |67.3% (57.1%, 76.5%) |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Worst-Case Specificity              |87.7% (81.7%, 92.3%) |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Worst-Case Youden's J               |0.55 (0.45, 0.66)    |
dx_itd_table(fit)
